messages.author: 872b7858ea2488c0
messages.subject: Trouble shooting for gl.sim.offspring
parts:
Hey guys,

I am trying to simulate offspring to generate thresholds of relatedness for fullsibs and halfsibs and I can't seem to get it to work.

The code I used is:

ggbf<-gl.read.dart(filename="Report_DLit19-4218_2_moreOrders_SNP_2_correctlabels.csv"
                   ,"ind_metrics_ggbf.csv")

ggbf<-gl.filter.repavg(ggbf,threshold=1.0,verbose=2)
ggbf<-gl.filter.callrate(ggbf,method="loc",threshold=0.98,mono.rm=TRUE,recalc=TRUE,plot=FALSE,verbose=2)

indNames(ggbf)

ggbfmales<-gl.keep.ind(ggbf,ind.list = c("BP2019_CB18M","BP2019_DL14M","BP2019_RU3M"))
ggbffemales<-gl.keep.ind(ggbf,ind.list = c("BP2019_RU7F","BP2019_CB21F","BP2019_DL2F"))


offsim<-gl.sim.offspring(ggbfmales, ggbffemales, noffpermother=10, sexratio = 0.5)

And the error message I got was:

Error in sample.int(length(x), size, replace, prob) : 
  vector size cannot be NA

Any help with troubleshooting this would be greatly appreciated. Thanks in advanced and happy New Year for Wednesday!

Cheers,
Chad

messages.subject: Re: Trouble shooting for gl.sim.offspring
parts:
Hi Chad,

The script does not appear to trap the case where their are no hets in either the sample of genotypes from the father, or the sample of genotypes from the mother used to simulate the offspring.

test <- gl.sim.offspring(testset.gl, testset.gl, noffpermother=10, sexratio = 0.5)

throws the error also.

I am afraid that fixing this, is going to have to wait until after the holiday period when the author of the script returns.

I have had a go at it, but do not fully understand the code. Revised script attached. You could try this, but should test it before use.

A

  noff <- nInd(mothers)*noffpermother
  mother <- sample(1:nInd(mothers),noff, replace = T)
  father <- sample(1:nInd(fathers), noff, replace = T)
 
  mmat <- as.matrix(mothers)[mother,]
  mhet <- sum(mmat==1)
  if(!is.na(mhet)){
     mother.half <- ifelse(mmat==1, sample(c(0,2), mhet, replace = T), mmat)
  } else {
    mother.half <- mmat
  }

Ditto for the fathers
